rules.name: parity-split thread criterion (exact, proved: Lemma 5 + Theorem 12)
rules.description_text: Let A=prod[a_i]_q, D=deg A, delta_j=A_j-A_{j-1} (0 outside), c0=(D+1)/2, F=sum floor(a_i/r). For each unordered pair {rho,sigma} of residues mod r with sigma = D+1-rho (mod r) and rho != sigma (a 'thread'), list ALL integers y<c0 congruent to rho or sigma in decreasing order y_0>y_1>y_2>... (continue into negative integers, where delta=0), put d_i=delta_{y_i}, V_0=0, V_{m+1}=d_m-V_m. Then P_b=A[b]_{q^r} is unimodal iff for every thread: V_b>=0 if b==F (mod 2), and V_{b-1}+d_b>=0 if b!=F (mod 2). (Residues with sigma=rho never fail.) Equivalently, without the parity split: V_b>=0 and V_{b-1}+d_b>=0 for every thread.

proofs.statement: Exact thread criterion: for b>=1, P_b is unimodal iff for every thread V_b>=0 and V_{b-1}+d_b>=0. Parity split: if b==F (mod 2) only V_b>=0 can fail; if b!=F only V_{b-1}+d_b>=0 can fail. In Theorem A terms: for b==F only the h_m<=h_{K-m} with K-2m<r can fail, and for b!=F only those with r<K-2m<2r can fail (Lemmas 3-11, Theorem 12, Remark 12a)
S2 (i): if b in U and b==F (mod 2) then b+1 in U. Hence when r divides no a_i, max U == 1+F (mod 2) (Theorem 13, Corollary 16)

Step-2 closure for all r and a_i: b in U, b>=3 implies b-2 in U. So U intersected with each parity class is an initial segment, and S2 (ii) holds for every b==F (mod 2) and for every b' of the same parity as b (Theorem 14, Corollary 16)
U is finite iff r divides no a_i (this reproves Cor 4.3) (Theorem 15)

Auxiliary results: delta=(1-q)prod[a_i]_q is weakly unimodal on the integers below (D+1)/2 (Lemma 3); for R=prod[rho_i]_q, the wrap of (1-q)R mod q^r-1 is >=0 on the half-period ((E+1-r)/2,(E+1)/2) (Lemma 8)

Conditional (C): let j*=B_off+2. If some thread with V_{j*}<0 satisfies d_{j*}-d_{j*+1}>=d_{j*+3}, then B*<=B_off+3 and S2 holds. In particular S2 holds whenever B_off>=F+e-4, with e=floor((E+1)/r) and E=sum(a_i mod r)-k (Theorem 17)

failure_report:
S2 is not fully proved. (i) is proved, and so is every part of (ii) except one inequality.

What remains: for b in U with b != F (mod 2) and b>=4, show b-3 is in U. Equivalently, show B_off >= B*-3, where B_off is the largest element of U with parity F.

How it reduces: by the thread criterion (Theorem 12), this is a statement about each thread separately. For j == F (mod 2) with V_j<0, it requires V_j < d_j - d_{j+1} - d_{j+3}. It would follow from inequality L': d_j - d_{j+1} >= d_{j+3} at the first off-parity failure. In positions this reads delta_u - delta_v >= delta_{v-r}, where v<u<v+r are consecutive thread positions.

Why the proved lemmas are not enough: unimodality of delta plus the sign lemma do not imply (C). The abstract sequence d=(2,1,1,1,1,1) with F even satisfies both lemmas but violates (C). Over all abstract unimodal sequences of length up to 7 with entries up to 4, 82 of 8659 violate it (abstract_thread.py). A proof therefore needs quantitative arithmetic of (1-q)prod[a_i]_q: an off-parity failure must never happen at a level where delta grows slowly.

How big the gap is: a pure exponential model delta=e^{lambda y}, with thread gaps g and r-g, has a violation window exactly when e^{-lambda g}(1+e^{-lambda r})>1, roughly lambda<1/(r+2g). No instance in the fit box comes close:
- L' held at all 3270 high failures checked, with minimum ratio 1.67e5.
- Inside the fit box (Theorem 17 coverage), failures fall at the very bottom of the thread in all 100488 exhaustive sets and in 1277 of 1500 random ones.
- Large-k instances can fail high (height 9 for r=30, a=[15]^40), but there delta grows very fast.

Evidence for S2 itself: 0 violations in 100488 exhaustive and 12000 random sets.

Fit-box incident: bigk.py once built thr2.Thr for (r=30, a=[14]*30+[16]*30). That is k=60 with unequal a_i, which is outside the box. It computed A and g before an assertion stopped the run; nothing was printed or used. Assertions now guard every instance constructor.

rules.name: S3* (refinement of S2 with explicit B and single undecided value decided by pair condition)
rules.description_text: If r divides some a_i: unimodal. Otherwise let d_y be the coefficients of the power series A(q)(1-q)/(1-q^r), A=prod[a_i]_q of degree D; tau_t = sum of coefficients of (1-q)A in residue class t mod r; y* = least y with d_y<0; B = 1+floor((2y*-D-1)/r). Predict: b>B -> not unimodal (proved, Lemma 10 of proof file); b<=B and b != B-1 -> unimodal (conjecture S3*); b = B-1 -> unimodal iff for all integers 0<=x<K/2 (K=D+1-r(b+1)): d_{K-x} - tau_{(K-x) mod r} >= d_x.

proofs.statement: Theorem R (reduction via peeling): let r divide no a_i, rho = residue multiset of a, sigma = sum(rho_i-1), d = coefficients of A(1-q)/(1-q^r), tau = residue-class sums of (1-q)A, Q_u = d_u - tau_{u mod r}, ND(K): Q_{K-x} >= d_x for all x with K-r <= 2x < K, mu*_inf = max{u: f_u < tau_u} where f = coefficients of 1/((1-q)^{k-1}(1-q^r)). If (TP_rho) every z with Q^rho_z<0 has floor((sigma+1-2z)/r) even, (E_rho) ND_rho(K) for all K = sigma+1 mod 2r with 2mu*_inf <= K <= sigma+1-2r, and (O_rho) ND_rho(K) for all K = sigma+1+r mod 2r with 2mu*_inf+3r <= K <= sigma+1-2r, then S2 holds for a, for all part sizes. Key lemmas: pair criterion (unimodal iff Q_{K-x}>=d_x for x>=1-rb, 2x<K, K=D+1-r(b+1)); LCW (if b-1 unimodal, only near-diagonal pairs matter); lifting a_i->a_i+r leaves tau and K_j=sigma+1-r(j+2) unchanged, adds a palindromic unimodal shift to d, so preserves ND and shrinks the bad set; d^a <= f (large-part limit); unimodal => K >= 2mu*(a). Corollaries (Theorem R + finite exact computation): S2 holds for every a with r<=30 whose residue multiset lies in the swept range (e.g. k<=40 for r<=5, k<=19 for r=7, k<=4 for r=28..30, all-congruent parts k<=60), with any part sizes; and for every a with r<=12 having at most 5 parts with residue in [2,r-1] (any number of parts that are 1 mod r, any sizes).

failure_report: This is a partial proof, not a proof of S2 for all parameters. The peeling path proves that S2 follows from a residue-level certificate: three finite statements (TP_rho, E_rho, O_rho) about the small-part instance rho, with all parts below r. Lifting (Theorem B) shows that the part sizes never matter. What is not done is a proof of that certificate for every rho; the attempt to prove it by adding one small part at a time did not close. Adding a part [s]_q convolves d, tau and Q with s ones. That turns ND(K') into a mix of pair conditions at the sums K'-2i for i<s, and these fall in both residue classes of K mod 2r. Only one class (E) holds for every K; the other (O) holds only above 2mu*+3r. So a single-part induction loses the parity bookkeeping. The certificate holds for all 3,154,273 rho swept (0 failures). The k-independent strong version, which covers any number of parts that are 1 mod r, fails for 25,737 of 1,547,599 long rho', so it cannot serve as the universal residue statement. Every failure has many parts: there are none with k'<=5 for r<=12 or k'<=3 for r<=30. Proving TP/E/O for all rho, for example from cyclic unimodality of prod[rho_i] mod (q^r-1) (0 failures in test_cyclic_unimodal.py, unproved), remains open.

proofs.statement: THEOREM 1 (proved). Let r>=2 divide no a_i, and let U = {b : A(q)[b]_{q^r} unimodal}. Then there are sigma>=1 and tau*>=sigma+2, both congruent to 1+F mod 2, such that U = [1,sigma] union {sigma+2, sigma+4, ..., tau*-2}. COROLLARIES (proved): (a) S2(i): if b is in U and b-1-F is odd, then b+1 is in U. (b) max U is congruent to 1+F mod 2. (c) If b is in U, then b-2 is in U. (d) S2 holds iff tau* <= sigma+4. Ingredients: Lemma 3 (e = centred (1-q)A is nonnegative and unimodal on the positive half; induction on k with a sign-pattern argument). Lemma 4 (exact zigzag criterion: U is the intersection over class pairs +-delta of {b : A_{b-1}>=0 and E_b+A_{b-2}>=0}, where E_j are e-samples on the positive points congruent to +-delta mod r and A_s are their alternating partial sums). Lemma 5 (each U_delta = [1,s0] union {s0+2,...,t1-2}). Lemmas 6-7 (arc-overlap lemma on Z_r, so the class sums of A are cyclically unimodal and peaked at S/2). Lemma 8 (sign rule (-1)^F * class-sum >= 0, which fixes the parity of s0). NOT PROVED: tau* <= sigma+4.

failure_report:
S2 is only partly proved. The part still open is the odd shift b -> b-3 in S2(ii).

What is proved (see proof_S2_partial.txt):
- U = [1,sigma] u {sigma+2, sigma+4, ..., tau*-2}, with sigma and tau* both congruent to 1+F mod 2 and tau* >= sigma+2.
- From this: S2(i) holds; max U is congruent to 1+F mod 2; U is closed under b -> b-2; and S2 is equivalent to tau* <= sigma+4.

How the proof goes:
- Two pairing arguments on the centred difference sequence e: Lemma 3 shows e is unimodal on the positive half; Lemma 4 is the exact zigzag criterion over class pairs +-delta.
- Lemma 7 (new) shows the class sums of prod[a_i] are cyclically unimodal, peaked at S/2. Its proof uses an arc-overlap lemma on Z_r. Lemma 8 turns this into the sign rule that fixes all parities.

Where it breaks: for each class pair delta, the shape of U_delta needs (Z2): A_{s0+2} + E_{s0+4} < 0, with s0 the first index where the alternating sum A_s goes negative.
- The paired identity Q_{s0} = E_{s0} + A_{s0-2} >= 0 only gives t1 >= s0+2. The needed bound t1 <= s0+4 cannot come from pairing alone.
- e-unimodality plus cyclic unimodality are not enough for the S2 shape. They fail on 102/2312 generic symmetric A, and on 226/10859 generic log-concave A (generic_cu.py, generic_cu_lc.py). So any proof of (Z2) must use quantitative product structure: it has to compare the class sum |tilde-tau(delta)| with the e-samples near the end of the support.
- The easy route s0 >= L-3 (which would make E_{s0+4}=0) is false. In the large-k stress set it fails in 495/1944 cases, with s0-L as low as -8.
- The robust inequality E_{s0+1} >= E_{s0+2} + E_{s0+4} holds at s0 in 1847/1847 cases. But it fails as a uniform lemma: its validity threshold sbar lies up to 28 steps past the E-peak. It would therefore need a separate proof that s0 >= sbar, which is no easier.

Empirically (Z2) holds everywhere tested: 0 failures in 5552 + 1944 class-pair instances. Also tau*-sigma is always 2 or 4 on 20233 instances, and s_neg - s0 is always 0 or 2 on 1705 instances. A proof of (Z2) would finish S2 with no other changes.

Near-miss structure. Let nneg(b) be the number of descents of P in its first half. In 307,589 instances checked (all gap sets plus 7 random families), nneg(b) >= nneg(b-2) and nneg(b+1) <= nneg(b) for b-1-F odd held with 0 breaks; these relations imply S2. Also 0 breaks in 441,970 adversarial hill-climb evaluations. The closest near-misses: the parity-flip candidate b=B*+1 often fails by exactly 1 descent, with nneg(B*+1)=nneg(B*+2). Any b >= B*+2 whose joining U would create a second missing point needed at least 2 descents.

Evaluators validated: core.margins agrees with tools/uni on 23,980 cases, and s2big (512-bit) agrees with tools/uni on 10,404 cases and with Python big-int results on 4,000 equal-family instances. s2enum2 gap and violation counts match s2big on 4 complete configurations.

failure_report:
I found no counterexample to S2 anywhere in the fit box (0 violations in about 659M exact evaluations). Everything is in /tmp/claude-0/qu/explore2/R2E4/.

Coverage:
- All-equal family: complete in the box.
- Two-value family: complete up to k<=14.
- Exhaustive multiset sweeps: 646.5M instances over all r=4..30 and k=3..40, but only for small value ranges at larger k.
- Random families: many middle residues; composite r in {12,24,30}; a_i near multiples of r; many 1s plus a few large entries.
- One- and two-change neighbourhoods of about 190k gap instances.
- Three hill-climbing objectives: 1.94M evaluations.

Not covered exhaustively: large k with large, mixed a_i (only sampled and hill-climbed). The many-1s family is degenerate because [1]_q=1, so those 1s change nothing.

The near-miss metrics based on normalized coefficient margins were scale-dependent: they drift towards large a_i, so I discarded them. Descent counts were the informative measure. Every gap seen has pattern 1^j 0 1 on (F,T6] with j odd. Two stronger descent-count relations, which together imply S2, were never broken. Bad candidates fail in matched pairs (b, b+1) with b-1-F odd, which is consistent with S2(i).
